newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby out as remarketing agent in Alameda, Calif.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby out as remarketing agent in Alameda, Calif.

text.p: Grigsby Brandford & Co Inc has been removed as a remarketing agent for commercial paper issued to renovate two Alameda County, Calif., sports facilities, a top county official said on Thursday.
The Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum Authority has begun to search for a firm to replace Grigsby Brandford, Alameda County's auditor-controller, Patrick O'Connell, said.
In recent weeks, Grigsby Brandford has undergone a dramatic shake-up, losing many employees including Napoleon Brandford and Suzanne Shank, who were two senior Grigsby Brandford officials.
Calvin Grigsby, the head of the firm now named Grigsby & Associates, was not immediately available for comment.

Grigsby Brandford had been selected as remarketing agent for about $160 million of the authority's debt, approximately half of the variable-rate commercial paper issued for football and basketball stadium renovations. Goldman Sachs was selected as remarketing agent for the other half, O'Connell said.
But in early October, Grigsby Brandford told the authority that it could not remarket $60 million of commercial paper as planned and urged the authority to find another firm.

In response, O'Connell said the Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum Authority removed Grigsby Brandford as remarketing agent on the deal and turned to Goldman Sachs, which remarketed the $60 million of commercial paper.
O'Connell said Goldman would carry out the remarketing in Grigsby's place for 60 days while the authority seeks a more permanent replacement.
Requests for proposals are expected to be mailed out in the coming days, O'Connell said. The authority hopes to have a new remarketing agent in place by early December, he added.

The management shake-up at Grigsby Brandford, then the nation's largest minority-owned investment banking firm, began on September 17, when Grigsby, the firm's founder and long-time chairman, abruptly announced his resignation.
After he left, it was disclosed that authorities were investigating bond deals the firm handled in Dade County, Fla. Grigsby has not been charged with any wrongdoing in the probe.
Without explanation, Grigsby decided earlier this month to rejoin his investment banking firm, known now as Grigsby & Associates.
